person: Grace is a 59-year-old retired librarian who married Walter Ashby, a retired surveyor, on 16 August. She is slowly changing her name to Ashby-Lindqvist, and Walter has chosen to take the same name. She is also the court-appointed representative of her mother's estate, three states away, and her mother died this month, so she is tired and grieving and wants only one gentle step at a time. She works a few hours a week at a historical society and uses her laptop and email slowly. She has a flight to her mother's town in late November and a January trip to see Walter's daughter in Dublin. She does not want the estate's accounts or her mother's papers confused with her own name change.
stated_up_front: Hello, I'm sorry, I'm not very quick with this. Walter and I married in August and I need to change my name on everything, and I'd like to start with whatever has to come first. There is a great deal going on with my mother's estate too, so please go slowly.

facts.truth: 16 August, at the county courthouse; she has the certified copy in a blue folder
Both Grace and Walter are taking Ashby-Lindqvist, hyphenated, with the same spelling on everything
It has shown Ashby-Lindqvist since 6 October, and her new card arrived on 14 October
It still shows Walter James Ashby; he has not applied, and he would go in person to the field office in Dunmore
It is a standard licence, not REAL ID, and expires in March 2028. She needs REAL ID for her 24 November flight to her mother's town
It was issued on 12 January 2026 in her old name, so it is under a year old. She leaves for Dublin on 28 January
She has a checking and a savings account at Harbor Credit Union in her own name. Walter has a separate checking account there
It is an estate checking account titled 'Estate of Margit Lindqvist', which she holds as representative. It must not be renamed
She works 12 hours a week at the Millbrook Historical Society, which pays her through PayPoint under her old name
It is booked on an airline site in her old name at about $740, and she has not touched it
Her sister Karin in Spokane phones her every Sunday, and Walter helps with the laptop

unknowns: Whether the DMV will accept her Social Security letter or insist on the new card itself
Which passport form applies and whether it costs anything, since she has only heard it might be free
How long the passport will be away, and whether it comes back before 28 January
Whether the historical society's payroll needs a copy of her new card or whether the Social Security update is enough
Whether the credit union will treat Walter's name change separately from hers
